name: blackbox-cubature-v3.1
title: 高斯测度下分段光滑函数的黑盒积分（理论 + 实验，v3.1）
status_reason: v3 after the GPT-6.2 Sol trial (analysis/DUAL_PLAN.md 9.8-9.9): instances that cannot be identified within the budget. Hard track: anisotropic quadratic forms with random spectra (generalized chi-square references, Ruben routes, Imhof/direct checks). Option track: single-asset local-volatility Euler models with random smooth volatility (backward Nystrom references) in place of the GBM families. Sample oracle capped at 2^18 points per sample per attempt; the statement describes the classes without naming parametric forms. Same protocol, score, references and image as v3. Trial runs only; not on the board.

data.public: versions/v3.1/data/public/instances.json (feedback set, 20 instances; internal repository only)
data.private: versions/v3.1/data/private/instances.json (formal set, 108 instances; internal repository only)

scoring.raw: G: two-track mean of family means of cell means of per-instance gains g = clip(e_GPCA-RQMC - e, -2, 2), e = log10 relative error clipped to [e_floor, 0]
scoring.mapping: G >= 0: 50 + 25 G; G < 0: 50 (G - G0) / -G0, G0 = plain Monte Carlo's G on the same instances; any failed instance scores 0
scoring.theory: theory/THEORY.md reviewed separately against a rubric; not part of the program score

submission_note: Put an executable run.sh and the complete source in /workspace/submission, and the theory document in /workspace/submission/theory/THEORY.md. Each instance runs ./run.sh in a fresh process with a read-only copy of the submission (only /tmp and the home directory are writable, and they are wiped between instances), speaking the JSON Lines protocol of problem.md on stdin/stdout.
instruction: Read /workspace/problem.md and /workspace/THEORY_APPENDIX.md in full, and look at /workspace/samples, /workspace/tools and /workspace/examples. Write the cubature program and the theory document described there.

feedback.note: Any failed, timed-out or protocol-violating instance makes the final program score 0. A category score compares the instances of one family with the reference in the same way as the final score. The theory document gets no feedback.
